Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Charlotte Biggs (author, Wikidata Q72085094), died 1827; John Gifford (editor, Wikidata Q6235288), died 1818. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Biggs, Charlotte, 1763?-1827; Gifford, John, 1758-1818 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: A residence in France, during the years 1792, 1793, 1794, and 1795; described in a series of letters from an English lady: with general and incidental remarks...  1797: Vol 1, 1797, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/bim_eighteenth-century_a-residence-in-france-d_1797_1. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 85%, 88%, 92% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Charlotte Biggs, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
